question: The _______ of a country is measured by the development of manufacturing industries.
solution:
The correct answer is__** economic strength.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The economic strength of a country is measured by the development of manufacturing industries because it contributes to the country's GDP and provides employment opportunities to the people.**
 
• Manufacturing industries also help in the growth of other sectors such as **transportation, communication, and services.**
 
• Debt, expenditure, and liability are not measures of** economic strength but rather financial obligations or expenses that a country incurs.**
 
• Debt is the amount of money a country owes to** lenders, expenditure is the amount of money spent on goods and services, and liability is the financial obligations of a country.**
 
• While these factors are important for a country's financial health, they do not directly contribute to its economic strength.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** **** Debt:** It is the amount of money a country owes to lenders, both domestic and foreign. 

 
 
• It can be used to finance government spending, but too much debt can lead to financial instability and can negatively affect a country's credit rating.
 
 
 
• ** Expenditure: I**t refers to the amount of money a country spends on goods and services, both for consumption and investment purposes.
 
 
• It includes both government and private spending.
 
 
 
• ** Liability: **It refers to the financial obligations of a country, including both short-term and long-term debt, as well as future obligations such as pensions and other entitlements.
 
 
• It is an important measure of a country's financial health as it indicates its ability to meet its financial obligations.
